rationale: Agomelatine (MT1/MT2 agonist, 5-HT2C antagonist; t½ ~2h; no discontinuation syndrome; no serotonergic reuptake activity) to sertraline (SSRI). Agomelatine clears within hours — no washout needed. No pharmacodynamic serotonin overlap hazard. Agomelatine can be stopped the same day sertraline is started. A brief 7-day overlap is used for clinical comfort and LFT exit monitoring. Sertraline has a favourable interaction profile — no CYP1A2 inhibition concerns. Exit LFTs should be checked before stopping agomelatine. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

schedule.notes: Start sertraline 50 mg. Continue agomelatine 25 mg nocte. Check exit LFTs (agomelatine final hepatotoxicity monitoring check). Sertraline: start at 50 mg, GI side effects common in first 1–2 weeks — take with food.
Stop agomelatine. Continue sertraline 50 mg. No discontinuation syndrome from agomelatine. Titrate sertraline to 100 mg at 4 weeks if response inadequate.

doseRatios.equivalencyNote: Agomelatine 25 mg ≈ sertraline 50 mg (standard effective starting doses for MDD). Different mechanisms — not pharmacologically equivalent. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.
